concerns.text: T032a (Baseline-Guava visual) and T032b (Oracle-Symbolic) are listed as parallel tasks, but T036 (Permutation Test) and T037 (Evaluation Results) depend on BOTH outputs. The current ordering implies T036 can run before T032a/b complete. T036 must be explicitly ordered AFTER both T032a and T032b to satisfy the 'Producer before Consumer' rule for the statistical comparison.

T023 (LoRA fine-tuning) and T027 (Inference on symbolic JSON) are marked [P] (parallel-safe). However, T027 (Inference) logically requires the model weights produced by T023 (Training) to be complete. Running T027 before T023 finishes would result in a crash or invalid inference on an untrained model. T027 must be moved to Phase 5 or explicitly sequenced after T023 completion.

T016 (Log perception ground truth) and T018 (Log latency) are marked [P] and listed as parallel to T014 (Transform symbolic). However, T016 and T018 consume the output of T014 (the symbolic observations) to generate logs. They cannot run in parallel with T014; they must follow T014. The [P] tag is incorrect here.

T010, T011, T012 (Tests) are marked [P] and listed before implementation tasks T013-T019. While TDD is a valid strategy, the 'Producer before Consumer' rule for the *execution* flow implies that the implementation (T013-T019) must exist before the tests (T010-T012) can be executed successfully. The current layout suggests parallel execution of tests against non-existent code, which is a semantic ordering violation for the 'run' phase.
